difficulty_reason: The proof runs a seven-way equivalence chase: (a)<=>(b) is the definition itself; (a)<=>(e) and (a)<=>(f) come from the permanence lemma's parts; (g) then follows formally; (c)<=> (b) needs a genuine construction — from (b) take the coproduct over x of the charts to build a diagram of type (c), using smooth locality on the target to see the coproduct h has P; finally (d): from (a), any diagram as in (d) has X \times_Y V \to V with P by smooth base change, so U \to V has P by \'etale precomposition stability; conversely (d) with U = X, V = Y gives (a). The web of reductions across seven statements is the substance.
